verses.1: And the mighty-armed Rama, having dismissed the bears, monkeys, and Rakshasas, was very happy and rejoiced greatly along with his brothers.
verses.2: Then, in the afternoon, Rama, along with his brothers, heard a sweet voice spoken from the sky.
verses.3: O gentle Rama, look at me with a gentle face; know me, O Lord, to be the Pushpaka chariot that has arrived from Kubera's abode.
verses.4: O best among men, having understood your command, I went to his abode to serve, and he (Kubera) spoke to me in return.
verses.5: He said, "You have been conquered by the great-souled king Rama, the descendant of Raghu, who slew the formidable Ravana, the lord of Rakshasas, in battle."
verses.6: He further said, "My supreme joy also arises from the killing of that evil-minded Ravana, along with his retinue, sons, and relatives."
verses.7: He concluded, "Therefore, O gentle Pushpaka, since you were conquered by the supreme Rama in Lanka, you must carry him; I command you to do so."
verses.8: This is indeed my greatest desire, that you should carry Rama and the people on their journey; therefore, go forth without any anxiety.
verses.9: Having understood the command of the great-souled Kubera, I have arrived in your presence; therefore, wait for me without any apprehension.
verses.10: By Kubera's command, I am invisible to all beings and I move by my own power, obeying your command.
verses.11: Thus addressed by Pushpaka, the mighty Rama then spoke, having seen the Pushpaka aerial car returned again.
verses.12: If it is so, then welcome to you, O best of aerial cars, Pushpaka; due to the favor of Kubera, no impropriety shall befall us.
verses.13: Then, the mighty-armed Rama worshipped the Pushpaka chariot with parched grains, flowers, and fragrant incense.
verses.14: Rama then told the Pushpaka, "Depart now, and remember to return whenever I recall you; O gentle one, do not be afflicted with sorrow, and may there be no obstruction to your desired flight in any direction, like that of the Siddhas."
verses.15: Having been worshipped and dismissed by Rama with the words "So be it," the Pushpaka then departed from there towards its desired direction.
verses.16: After that Pushpaka, which was of good deeds, had thus disappeared, Bharata, with folded hands, spoke these words to Rama.
verses.17: O hero, while you rule, the utterances of non-human beings are repeatedly seen in various forms.
verses.18: O Raghava, this full month has passed without any disease among beings, and even for the aged, death does not come.
verses.19: Women give birth without illness, humans are healthy, and O King, the joy of the city dwellers is exceedingly great.
verses.20: The clouds rain nectar-like water at the proper time, and these winds blow, pleasant to the touch, agreeable, and auspicious.
verses.21: O King, the city and country dwellers say in the city, "May such a king be immortal!"
verses.22: Having heard these very sweet words spoken by Bharata, Rama, the best of kings, became filled with joy. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकचत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 41 ।। Thus ends the forty-first sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
